transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I keep getting these nagging thoughts that I’ve forgotten something important. Like maybe I left my aunt’s medicine out wrong, or I didn’t set up my classroom materials safely. Even when I’m pretty sure I handled it, the doubt just… keeps coming back.
When these thoughts come up, do you find yourself doing certain things over and over, like checking or counting, to try to ease the worry?

Yeah… I do check. Mostly before I leave the house or my classroom. I’ll go back over things a few times—the pill organizer, the stove, lesson plans… sometimes I just replay what I did in my head until I feel okay enough to leave. It’s not for hours or anything, but it can make me late.
Do these thoughts and the checking behaviors cause you a lot of stress or interfere with your daily life?

It does, a bit. I’m still doing what I need to do—work, family stuff—but mornings take longer than they should. Sometimes I get to school already feeling rushed, like I’m behind before anything’s even started.

And… lesson prep or journaling at night just doesn’t feel as easy or calming as it used to.
Do you ever feel like you have to do these checks, or do you feel some relief when you do them, even if you wish you didn't have to?

Yeah… I think I do feel like I have to. Before I leave, I’ll check the same things a few times—the pill organizer, the stove, my lesson plans—or I’ll kind of replay what I did in my head.

It does calm me down a little once I’ve done it, but… I don’t really want to need it. And sometimes it makes me late.
Do you ever have thoughts that pop into your mind that you don’t want or that bother you, like fears of harming someone accidentally or images that are upsetting?

Yeah… not really images, exactly. It’s more like this nagging thought that I forgot something important.

Like maybe I left my aunt’s medicine out wrong, or I didn’t set up something in my classroom safely. Even when I know I probably did it right, the doubt just kind of comes back.
Are these thoughts about forgetting something completely unwanted, and do they seem excessive or irrational to you, even while you’re having them?

Yes… they’re unwanted. I don’t sit there trying to think about it.

And I guess I do know it’s probably more than it needs to be. Like, I’ll know I handled my aunt’s medicine or got the classroom stuff set up safely, but the doubt still pops back in anyway. It feels excessive, even if I can’t quite shake it.
Do these doubts ever lead you to do things a certain way to feel more certain or to prevent something bad from happening, like following specific routines or needing things to be in order?

Yeah… I guess I do. I’ll go back over things before I leave, like the stove, my aunt’s pill organizer, or my lesson plans.

Sometimes I just replay what I did in my head until I feel… calm enough to go. It’s not a huge routine, but it can make me late sometimes.
When you have these nagging doubts, do you feel driven to perform certain mental acts or behaviors in a specific way to reduce the anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah… I think so. I’ll check the same things a few times before I leave, like the stove or my aunt’s pill organizer, or my lesson plans at school.

Sometimes I just go over it silently in my head until I feel settled enough to leave. It’s not… dramatic, but it does make me late sometimes.
Have these doubts and checking behaviors caused problems in any important areas of your life, like at work, with family, or in your social life?

A little, yeah. I mean, I’m still doing what I need to do… work, family stuff, all of that.

But mornings take longer than they should, and sometimes I get to school already feeling rushed or behind. And things like lesson prep, or even journaling at night, just don’t feel as smooth or calming as they used to.
Have you ever had thoughts, urges, or images that kept coming up and bothered you, even if they weren’t about forgetting something or making sure things are safe?

Not really outside of that, I don’t think. It’s mostly the same kind of doubt… like I forgot something important with my aunt’s medicine, or I didn’t set something up safely in my classroom.

Even when I know I probably did it, it just kind of pops back in my head and bothers me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with recurrent, intrusive, and unwanted thoughts centered around fears of having forgotten something important or not having completed tasks correctly (e.g., arranging pills, securing the stove, setting up classroom materials). These obsessions lead to repetitive behaviors (e.g., checking, mental review) aimed at reducing distress or preventing a feared event. The behaviors are time-consuming and cause clinically significant impairment in daily functioning, particularly in the morning routine and work preparation. Insight is preserved, with the patient recognizing the thoughts and behaviors as excessive. Duration is consistent with a chronic presentation, and there is no evidence of a primary mood episode or trauma-related symptoms.
